stories.headline: Max Verstappen tops final practice; starts São Paulo GP from back of grid
stories.summary: Max Verstappen edged out Kimi Antonelli to go quickest in the final practice session of the São Paulo Grand Prix.
stories.body:
Max Verstappen edged out Kimi Antonelli to go quickest in the final practice session of the São Paulo Grand Prix.

The Dutchman crossed the line 0.025 seconds quicker than new world champion Antonelli, but will be starting from the back of the grid for Sunday's race.

Verstappen had an all-new engine fitted to his Red Bull before the session.

Lando Norris, who has been looking quick in his heavily-upgraded McLaren, was over one-tenth off the pace.

Mercedes' George Russell was fourth-fastest and Ferrari's Charles Leclerc was behind in fifth.

Leclerc and teammate Lewis Hamilton will be taking a 10-place grid penalty for the race for taking new internal combustion engines.

Hamilton suffered issues inside the last 25 minutes of the session and returned to the garage. He finished in 12th.

- Charles Leclerc says 'everything is settled' after Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari crisis talks

- Haas boss confirms axing Esteban Ocon after Mexico was 'best interest of team'

- F1 to make a decision on season finale in Imola next week - sources

Russell is taking a five-place grid drop after his team fitted another new engine to his Mercedes.

McLaren's Oscar Piastri finished sixth-fastest, with Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad seventh and Liam Lawson eighth, respectively.

The weather started to turn towards the end of the session and rain could be on the way ahead of qualifying at 6 p.m. GMT / 1 p.m. ET.

stories.headline: Tottenham's winning run brought to abrupt end by late Noah Okafor winner
stories.summary: Noah Okafor stepped off the bench to snatch Leeds three points as they beat Tottenham 1-0 at Elland Road to snap their five-game winless Premier League run.
stories.body:
Noah Okafor stepped off the bench to snatch Leeds three points as they beat Tottenham 1-0 at Elland Road to snap their five-game winless Premier League run.

Okafor struck with his first touch, two minutes after replacing Lukas Nmecha, to seal Leeds' third league win of the season and condemn resurgent Tottenham to their first defeat in five.

The Londoners were chasing their fourth straight win having shot up the table from bottom to ninth place before kick-off, but in a game of few clear-cut chances Okafor's introduction proved decisive.

James Trafford gifted Bournemouth their opening goal last week with a misplaced pass, but he appeared to have put that behind him, cleanly catching an early cross and then picking out his man with a low clearance.

Trafford spoke this week of his "horrendous" spell at Manchester City last season, saying he had to leave for the sake of his mental wellbeing after playing second fiddle to Gianluigi Donnarumma.

But he is thriving in his number one role at Elland Road and after Ao Tanaka and Ethan Ampadu had fired off target, the England goalkeeper showed his confidence remains undiminished.

He punched clear a dangerous cross from Mohammed Kudus and, as Tottenham began to find their stride, saved well down to his right from Omar Marmoush's low shot.

Home fans appealed for a penalty when a cross appeared to hit Mateus Fernandes on the arm, but VAR ruled otherwise.

Leeds were wasteful with their balls into the box and they breathed a huge sigh of relief deep in the first half when a lengthy VAR check concluded no serious foul play after Jayden Bogle's studs had accidentally caught Mathys Tel on his Achilles.

After Nmecha, who made his first start of the season, had headed straight at Tottenham goalkeeper Antonín Kinsky, Tel was unable to continue and was replaced by Dominic Solanke.

Leeds stepped it up after the restart. Dominic Calvert-Lewin's header was blocked, Nico Elvedi nodded his follow-up wide and Tanaka fired over the crossbar.

A spell of concerted pressure from the home side raised the noise levels, with Nmecha crowded out after being played into the box.

Tottenham substitute Conor Gallagher flashed a 20-yard shot inches wide and, with the game on a knife's edge, Ampadu lashed over after Bogle's initial effort had been blocked.

Kinsky then produced the save of the match to tip Sean Longstaff's volley over the crossbar - the former Newcastle midfielder made his first league start in almost a year - as Leeds chased the winner.

Leeds boss Daniel Farke sent on Harry Wilson and Okafor for Tanaka and Nmecha with 13 minutes left and it proved a masterstroke as his side broke the deadlock two minutes later.

Wilson played in Okafor with his first touch following a long throw into the box and the Switzerland striker ran on to rifle his finish beyond Kinsky for his second league goal of the season.

Trafford ensured Leeds' win when he dived full length to keep out Jan Paul van Hecke's header from a late free-kick as Tottenham slipped to their second defeat in eight league games.

stories.headline: Fantasy football last-minute pickups: Kaelon Black and Malik Willis lead the way
stories.summary: If injuries, bye weeks or tough matchups have you seeking lineup help, Matt Bowen lists potential options.
stories.body:
At various points during the fantasy football season, injuries, bye weeks and breaking news can cause you to need reinforcements for your fantasy lineup. Every Friday throughout the 2026 NFL season, Matt Bowen will offer some late-week pickup options at each of the primary fantasy positions to help fill those holes, with an emphasis on deeper leagues.

Because of that, this column will focus mostly on players rostered in under 50% of ESPN leagues, with occasional exceptions.

Let's start the Week 9 list at the quarterback position with two players who have positive matchups (based on the numbers). After that, we will pivot to the wide receiver spot, and I've gone a little deeper than usual, with five pass catchers who bring stable floors to the lineup. I also have three running backs who can be played as flex in deeper leagues, plus a tight end who has quietly put together three straight weeks of quality production. As always, we'll end with D/ST, but it's pretty lean out there right now.

Quarterbacks

J.J. McCarthy, New York Giants (26.6% rostered; at Philadelphia Eagles)

McCarthy scored 10.18 points in Week 7, completing 20-of-28 for 252 yards. McCarthy failed to throw a touchdown, and the rushing totals were down (one carry, one yard), but he is seeing the field with speed and driving the ball from the pocket. With a matchup Sunday versus an Eagles defense that ranks in the bottom 10 versus quarterbacks, McCarthy has value in superflex formats.

Malik Willis, Miami Dolphins (18.4% rostered; vs. Detroit Lions)

Willis is averaging 19.8 points over his past three games, with multiple touchdown throws in two of them. Plus, he brings a dual-threat element to the lineup as Willis is averaging 32.1 yards rushing this season with a touchdown in two of his past three games. Given Willis' rising numbers, he's a smart play this week versus a Lions defense that has allowed a league-worst 24.8 points per game to opposing quarterbacks.

Wide receivers

Malik Washington, Miami Dolphins (39.4% rostered; vs. Detroit Lions)

Washington scored a season-high 15 points in Week 8 as he caught his first touchdown of the season. He's now posted double-digit points in four of his past five games. With his route/alignment versatility, Washington will also see rushing attempts, and he gets a quality matchup versus a Lions defense that ranks in the bottom five versus wide receivers.

Keenan Allen, Indianapolis Colts (44.3% rostered; vs. Dallas Cowboys)

I would take the matchup with Allen versus the Dallas defense Sunday. This Cowboys unit ranks in the bottom 10 versus wide receivers and Allen has scored 13 or more points in two of his past three games. The touchdown upside is limited with Allen, but he can still uncover and find space as an outlet. After catching all seven of his targets for 67 yards versus the Jaguars last week, Allen can be played as high-floor WR3.

Ryan Flournoy, Dallas Cowboys (24.3% rostered; at Indianapolis Colts)

I don't know why Flournoy's roster percentage is still down given his role as the No. 3 target for Dak Prescott -- behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens -- in the Dallas pass game. Flournoy has scored 10 or more points in four straight games with a touchdown reception in two. During this stretch, Flournoy has caught 17 of 21 targets for 238 yards. Get him in the lineup this week versus the Colts.

Antonio Williams, Washington Commanders (18.4% rostered; vs. Los Angeles Rams)

Williams gets a tougher matchup versus the Rams defense on Sunday, but I still see value here in deeper formats as a WR3. Williams scored 10 points in Week 7, catching a season-high five passes (on seven targets) for 54 yards. With Terry McLaurin (knee) out for the season, Williams' role will continue to increase, and he has the route savvy to win inside the numbers.

Demarcus Robinson, San Francisco 49ers (0.9% rostered; vs Las Vegas Raiders)

Robinson, who was activated off IR this week, could be in line to see volume Sunday versus the Raiders as Mike Evans (Achillies) is not expected to play. Robinson has played in only two games this season (Weeks 1 and 2), when he caught five of six targets for 84 yards and a touchdown. However, Robinson will have WR3 value with a steady role in Kyle Shanahan's offense.

Running backs

Devin Singletary, New York Giants (27.5% rostered; at Philadelphia Eagles)

With Tyrone Tracy Jr. (hamstring) on IR and Cam Skattebo (hamstring) doubtful for Sunday's game in Philly, Singletary elevates to the lead role in the Giants' backfield. In the Week 7 win over the Texans, Singletary scored a season-high 14.5 points, rushing for 41 yards and a touchdown on five carries and adding 14 receiving yards on three receptions. With his anticipated volume boost, plus the receiving upside he brings to the lineup, Singletary can be played as a RB2/Flex in Week 9.

Kaelon Black, San Francisco 49ers (27.8% rostered; vs. Las Vegas Raiders)

Managers should keep an eye on the status of Christian McCaffrey (hamstring), as Black could find himself in an elevated role Sunday versus the Raiders. If McCaffrey can go, Black still has value as a deeper league flex. Black has seen at least nine touches in each of his past two games, plus he rushed for 63 yards and a touchdown in the Week 7 game versus the Falcons.

Mike Washington Jr., Las Vegas Raiders (30.1% rostered; at San Francisco 49ers)

Washington led the Raiders backfield with 25 carries in the Week 8 win over the Jets, and while he didn't rush with much efficiency (3.3 YPC), he was the clear lead back over Ashton Jeanty (five total touches). We expect Jeanty to be back in the mix Sunday against the 49ers, but Washington will still get his looks in a shared backfield approach. He's a deeper-league flex here.

Tight end
Greg Dulcich, Miami Dolphins (3.7% rostered; vs. Lions)

Dulcich has quietly scored 10.5 points per game over his past three, with at least four receptions in each, and he gets a Lions defense that ranks dead last in the league versus tight ends. Given the available tight ends and the matchups, Dulcich has the best path to production in Week 9.

D/ST
New York Giants (33.4% rostered; at Eagles)

It's a struggle to find a quality defense rostered in under 50% of ESPN leagues this week, but the Giants could be in a positive spot here versus the Eagles, who are pivoting to Joe Milton at quarterback for Sunday's matchup. The Giants have taken the ball away only once in the past three games, but they have recorded at least one sack in three of the past four. View this move as a late-week flier (if you need one).

stories.headline: Fantasy basketball: Four players whose upgraded skill sets look real
stories.summary: Which players have added new dimensions to their game? Here are four who can sustain their newly-demonstrated skills.
stories.body:
Baseball analyst Ron Shandler famously posited that once a player has demonstrated a skill over a sufficiently meaningful sample, they own it. The key qualifier is that the skill must be demonstrated over a sustained period, not merely in an isolated performance or brief hot streak.

This concept applies to basketball as well. Once a player demonstrates they can effectively protect the rim over multiple months, we can assume they "own" that skill as part of their overall skill set. It was clear early in Walker Kessler's career with the Utah Jazz that he was a special rim protector -- a skill that has proved enduring.

We learn to trust what players can and cannot do on the court over time. Box scores create precedents. Past demonstrated ability deserves more weight than recent struggles because a skill can lie dormant without disappearing.

Which players are establishing new levels of expertise so far this season? Even with the sample size remaining quite small, we can begin to identify new identities around the league. With this lens in mind, let's discuss a quartet of players who have added new dimensions to their real and fantasy reputations thus far.

The prospect who was promised

Incredibly fun and prestigious player comparisons -- to the likes of Rashard Lewis and even Chris Bosh -- surfaced when Jabari Smith Jr. was evaluated during the 2022 NBA draft cycle. While those were lofty comparisons, they spoke to Smith's potential to go beyond a traditional "3-and-D" archetype and develop into a game-changing two-way force.

We're not quite at the All-Star tier for Smith, but it's becoming clear that he is taking ownership of a new level of shooting and scoring. Even though his shot diet this year is identical to last season's, he has leapt nearly 20% in scoring output thanks to appreciable spikes in shooting success. There is danger in simply trusting a hot streak. A more granular look shows Smith is finally thriving off the dribble and as a pull-up shooter, which is also showing up in his ability to initiate and finish drives.

Smith has already proven he owns a unique ability to protect the rim from an atypical position, as his career 2.5% block percentage reveals. The blend of improved shooting and scoring, along with his ability to create turnovers, has Smith positioned 20th overall on the Player Rater, just ahead of Houston Rockets teammate Alperen Sengun. Even when his outside shooting cools -- and it will -- Smith has leveled up enough to remain an impact player.

The ready rookie

Beyond being an amazing soundbite and the oldest prospect in his class, Yaxel Lendeborg was a somewhat mysterious prospect. Dominant rebounding numbers over a long college career did not necessarily indicate a dynamic offensive package.

Even just three weeks into his career, it's becoming clear that Lendeborg is an effective bully, sporting an awesome free throw rate of 46.4%. Free throw rate divides field goal attempts by free throw attempts to reveal the balance a player can sustain between creating fouls and shooting volume. This is the rate of a primary offensive engine for most teams.

Getting two feet in the paint is a skill, and Lendeborg is flashing it both in the eye test and statistically. The Golden State Warriors rookie is taking nearly a quarter of his shots from within three feet of the basket, sinking 68% of them. Producing free throws and efficient attempts in the paint are rare elements for a rookie's profile just eight starts into his career. If or when Lendeborg hits a slump in the coming weeks, it will be important to see whether he sustains these opportunity rates, even if he is not converting them.

The two-way sleeper

Possibly lost in the shuffle of the Washington Wizards' exciting rebuild has been the emergence of Kyshawn George as a two-way glue guy. Teams need connective, high-energy players willing to do a bit of everything. His current profile doesn't scream breakout, but he is a plus contributor across several categories -- the sum of his skills is greater than each addend.

The most exciting and seemingly enduring part of his rise this season has been his connection with Trae Young in pick-and-roll actions. Those plays have George finishing around the rim at the highest volume and efficiency of his career, aided by his nearly 6-foot-11 wingspan.

Shot diet is more revealing about a player -- and is a steadier, stickier data point at this point in the season -- than shooting results. Getting hot can happen over eight games, but the breakdown of where and how shots are taken becomes increasingly meaningful as minutes accumulate. George is taking 24.7% of his shots from within three feet of the basket this season and making 73% of them, compared to just 14.7% and 66%, respectively, over his first two pro seasons. Like Houston's Smith, George leverages his length in rim protection, sporting a career-best block percentage of 3.7%. Young is a maestro at making things easy for his roll partners, and George is currently enjoying the benefit.

The first 'Barrier Thief'

Yes, Dyson Daniels has earned the moniker "The Great Barrier Thief," but let's remember that the Los Angeles Lakers' Matisse Thybulle, also a member of the Australian Olympic team, is among the great steal artists of the era. Having led the NBA in steal percentage in his third season and averaged two steals per game over the past three seasons, there is no question that Thybulle is among the most larcenous defenders in the league.

What is aiding Thybulle's fantasy relevance is an expansion beyond being purely a defensive specialist. He is sinking two 3-pointers per game with a fun, new-look, no-dip 3-point shot that he gets off rapidly in catch-and-shoot scenarios. Like George, who is working so well off Young's high-value passes, Thybulle is getting fed wide-open looks in rhythm thanks to the gravity and generosity of Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves. Up to 69th on the Player Rater, it's possible that Thybulle delivers a top-100 season after being classified for years solely as a deep-league specialist.

stories.headline: NHL Tonight: Your guide to all 12 games on Saturday's schedule
stories.summary: Find game previews, betting intel, broadcast information, stats and highlights here.
stories.body:
There won't be another day when all 32 NHL teams are playing until April, but the league will be operating at 75% capacity on Saturday with 12 games on the schedule.

The slate of games offers a mixed bag of rivalries (new and old) along with a superb matchup of two teams that have a high chance of meeting in the Stanley Cup Final.

Read on for a look at what you need to know for each game, including betting info and broadcast details.

Odds are provided by DraftKings and subject to change.

Florida Panthers at Washington Capitals

12:30 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | WSH -125, O/U: 6.5

The way that this season has shaped up thus far, these two teams could well be fighting for one wild-card playoff spot by season's end. This will be the first showdown between the clubs, after Florida won all three matchups last season by an aggregate score of 16-8.

The Capitals are still waiting for Alex Ovechkin to get rolling, as the NHL's all-time leading goal scorer has just one of them through 14 games. Instead, they've been paced by newcomer Alex Tuch, who has 10.

A familiar face leads the Panthers in scoring -- Matthew Tkachuk, who is possibly the most Panther of anyone who's ever Panthered, has 22 points in 16 games -- while Sam Reinhart and Carter Verhaeghe are tied for the team lead in goals with nine apiece.

St. Louis Blues at Nashville Predators

1 p.m. ET (NHL Network) | STL -115, O/U: 6.5

The Predators enter this Central Division showdown having won three games in a row against a murderers' row of top contenders: 5-4 over the Lightning (shootout), 4-1 over the Hurricanes and 3-2 over the Avalanche in overtime.

Nashville also won the last matchup between the two teams, 5-2 on Oct. 17. The Preds had five different goal scorers in that game and won despite racking up 10 penalty minutes to the Blues' two. Filip Forsberg leads the team with 19 points through 16 games, and Steven Stamkos leads in goals with nine.

The Blues have a balanced offensive attack -- with five players in double digits in scoring through 16 games -- but have yet to have anyone break out. Does that begin Saturday?

New York Rangers at Seattle Kraken

5 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | NYR -118, O/U: 6.5

To the surprise of many, these teams enter this matchup in third place in their respective divisions.

The Rangers are on a two-game winning streak and are led in scoring by defenseman Adam Fox (two goals, 19 assists in 17 games). The Long Island native is on pace for 104 points, which would break the franchise's single-season scoring record by a defenseman (Brian Leetch had 102 in 1991-92).

Seattle's assist leader is a familiar face to the visiting Rangers: Kaapo Kakko, who was their No. 2 pick in 2019. Kakko shares the team's scoring lead at 12 points with Berkly Catton and Chandler Stephenson.

Montreal Canadiens at Toronto Maple Leafs

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | MTL -115, O/U: 6.5

These two franchises have been playing each other since Dec. 26, 1917 -- i.e. during World War I. There have been 855 total meetings, and the Canadiens lead both the regular-season and playoff series.

Montreal has won the past four matchups between the teams, including a 3-2 victory on Opening Night (despite William Nylander's goal 48 seconds in).

No surprises here, the Habs are led in scoring this season by Lane Hutson (16 points in 16 games), Nick Suzuki (15 in 10) and Cole Caufield (15 in 16). But the real story is in goal, where Jacob Fowler's early play -- a 7-1-1 record, 2.17 goals-against average and .925 save percentage -- has him on the Calder Trophy short list.

For Toronto, captain Auston Matthews is back among the league leaders in scoring (26 points in 17 games), while Nylander is just outside the top 10. The goaltending from Sergei Bobrovsky and Anthony Stolarz has not been up to Fowler's level, but there's a lot of season left!

Utah Mammoth at Ottawa Senators

7 p.m. ET (NHL Network) | OTT -110, O/U: 6.5

In the everlasting "which NHL division is best?" debate, here's a data point: These teams enter this showdown with identical 10-6-1 records. The Mammoth are in second place in the Central, while the Senators are fourth in the Atlantic.

All of that aside, this is a chance for fans to see some of the NHL's elite (and sometimes overlooked) young talent hit the ice. That begins with Ottawa's Tim Stutzle, whose 22 points in 17 games have him tied for 11th on the NHL leaderboard.

One of the players with whom he's tied is Utah's Clayton Keller. And one point behind both of them is Logan Cooley, who scored another hat trick on Thursday to bring his career total to five in 228 games. That sets an NHL record for the lowest number of games to five hat tricks, two games fewer than the previous record holder, Ovechkin.

New Jersey Devils at New York Islanders

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | NJ - 148, O/U: 5.5

There's no official nickname for this NYC metro area rivalry -- unlike "Battle of New York" for Isles-Rangers and "Battle of the Hudson" for Devils-Rangers -- so maybe it's "Clash of the Commuters"?

Regardless, the two teams have had some explosive matchups throughout the past decades. The Isles hold the overall regular-season edge 155-89-32, while the Devils have won four head-to-head playoff series to the Isles' two.

The Islanders won the first game of this season's series 6-0 way back on Oct. 3, as Ilya Sorokin stopped all 37 shots the Devils fired at his cage.

Of course, those were the pre-Connor Hellebuyck Devils. Does the involvement of the former Hart and Vezina Trophy winner change anything this time around?

Chicago Blackhawks at Carolina Hurricanes

8 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | CAR -395, O/U: 6.5

The Canes enter this game having lost just five games total (two of which came after regulation) out of 16 contests, while the Blackhawks have just four wins in 17 tries. And that includes a 5-2 win for the Canes on Oct. 10 in Chicago. Ergo that massive moneyline.

One big thing to watch for Carolina is whether this game marks the return of defenseman Alexander Nikishin, who was re-signed recently after an extended holdout. The Canes just got forward Taylor Hall back in the lineup after his early-season injury and are still waiting on the return of captain Jordan Staal, who is on IR with a calf injury. (Yes, the Canes have been rolling everyone while missing key players.)

Chicago is without Patrick Kane and Bowen Byram, the latter of whom played just six games after coming over in a major offseason trade. Connor Bedard leads the Blackhawks in scoring (12 points in 11 games), while rookie Roman Kantserov paces the club in goals (eight).

San Jose Sharks at Dallas Stars

8 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | DAL -290, O/U: 6.5

Less than 24 hours after a loss against the Central Division-leading Wild on Friday, the puck drops on a showdown with another powerhouse in Dallas.

San Jose has failed to launch this season; amid many predicting a playoff run for Macklin Celebrini & Co. this spring, they're currently jockeying for fifth in the Pacific with the rebuilding Calgary Flames, losing six of their past seven.

Dallas has been a team of streaks this season: It began the campaign losing two, then won two, then lost another two, then won five, then lost two, then (you guessed it) won two more before a loss Thursday to Columbus. It would appear the Stars are "due" for another loss -- or can they break the cycle?

Tampa Bay Lightning at Minnesota Wild

8 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | TB -122, O/U: 6.5

For a pairing of teams that we might well see square off in the 2027 Stanley Cup Final, it's a little disappointing that both matchups are taking place so early in the season, but here we are.

The Lightning won their first meeting 3-2 on Oct. 8. That game was the John Carlson Show, as the veteran defenseman scored twice to lead the way. Dennis Hildeby was in the crease for Tampa in that game, stopping 34 of 36 Minnesota shots. Winger Nikita Kucherov requested a trade but keeps scoring nonetheless with 20 points through 15 games.

Since the loss to Tampa, Minnesota has gone 10-2-2, largely thanks to the play of goaltender Jesper Wallstedt. Overall, the 23-year-old Swede is 11-2-3, with a 1.99 GAA and .922 SV% (tops in the league in wins, and among the top 10 in the ratios). The Wild also have two of the best players at their respective positions in the league in winger Kirill Kaprizov (16 goals in 18 games) and defenseman Quinn Hughes (25 points in 18 games).

Will we see these two again in the Cup Final? Stathletes projections give the pairing a 2.48% chance, which is 11th highest.

Detroit Red Wings at Colorado Avalanche

9 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | COL -225, O/U: 6.5

One of the most iconic rivalries of the past few decades -- you are required to watch this documentary if you have not yet -- has lost a fair amount of luster as the Red Wings have fallen off (and moved back to the Eastern Conference).

The Avs have gone 6-1-1 at home this season and hope to keep adding to that first column here. Nathan MacKinnon paces the team in scoring (and is fifth in the NHL) with 27 points through 17 games. Cale Makar -- whose game-changing $20.8 million AAV contract extension kicks in next season -- has 18 through 16.

Detroit doesn't have anyone to challenge MacKinnon that high up the leaderboard, but six players have hit double digits in points through 17 games, including 16 apiece for Lucas Raymond and Alex DeBrincat.

Pittsburgh Penguins at Los Angeles Kings

9 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | LA -135, O/U: 6.5

After playoff appearances by both of these teams in 2026, the postseason now seems like a distant fantasy. Each team enters the game with 12 points. But hey, one win can start a streak and get them back on track!

Sidney Crosby enters this matchup with a five-game scoring streak against the Kings. It's not Crosby, but Erik Karlsson who leads the Pens in scoring this season with 16 points in 16 games.

L.A.'s Artemi Panarin is one point ahead of Karlsson in two fewer games, and he has 46 points (19 goals, 27 assists) in 36 career regular-season games against the Penguins (skating for the Blackhawks, Blue Jackets and Rangers).

Vancouver Canucks at Edmonton Oilers

10 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | EDM -310, O/U: 6.5

If nothing else, this game should be entertaining -- unless you like low-scoring affairs. These clubs have played twice already, with final scores of 6-5 Canucks and 9-7 Oilers.

Following that season-opening win against Edmonton, Vancouver has won just two additional games in 17 tries. The Canucks have also yet to match the six-goal total since. But maybe this is the opportunity for leading scorer Elias Pettersson (18 points in 18 games) & Co.

We are all aware of what the Oilers have been up to on the score sheets, as Connor McDavid (44 points), Leon Draisaitl (31) and Evan Bouchard (30) are 1-2-3 on the league's scoring leaderboard. How much will they be padding those totals in this contest?

Reminder: Fans can catch all the action in the NHL streaming hub and on the ESPN App.

Today in hockey history
What would the sport of hockey be without ice? (Well, field hockey.) In any event, indoor ice rinks are pretty important for the past, present and future of ice hockey, and there was a significant development on that front on this date in history.

On Nov. 7, 1896, the St. Nicholas Rink opened on the northeast corner of 66th Street and Columbus Ave. in New York, built by a consortium that included Cornelius Vanderbilt and John Jacob Astor.

The St. Nicholas Hockey Club called the building home, and the rink would host the first matchup in ice hockey between Harvard and Yale, as well as the first matchup between women's ice hockey teams in the U.S.

Eventually, the more lucrative sport of boxing took over the arena, and so hockey moved elsewhere in Manhattan. But the St. Nicholas Rink was a critical step in the evolution of indoor ice facilities.

stories.headline: Witness: Clase 'inside' pitch info dried up amid Mizuhara case fallout
stories.summary: A witness said that the inside info he used to bet on Clase pitches dried up due to increased scrutiny from the scandal involving Shohei Ohtani's interpreter.
stories.body:
NEW YORK -- A government witness testified Friday in the federal trial of Cleveland Guardians pitchers Emmanuel Clase and Luis Ortiz that the inside information he used to bet regularly on Clase pitches in 2023 dried up the next season due to increased scrutiny from the gambling scandal involving Shohei Ohtani's interpreter at the time.

Luis de Aza Baez said he placed dozens of bets and won thousands of dollars by wagering on the velocity of select Clase pitches during the 2023 season, "because I had inside information." Clase is accused of conspiring with bettors to rig 18 pitches over three seasons.

De Aza Baez said that when he asked for more information on Clase pitches in 2024, he was told that because of "what was going on with Ohtani, there was no more information like that."

Ohtani, the Los Angeles Dodgers' superstar, came under scrutiny in March 2024 after ESPN reported that millions of dollars had been sent from his bank account to an illegal bookmaking operation. His longtime interpreter, Ippei Mizuhara, later pleaded guilty to stealing nearly $17 million from Ohtani to pay off gambling debts and is currently in prison. Ohtani was cleared of any wrongdoing.

De Aza Baez, who worked as an Uber driver, told prosecutors that he began receiving information about the pitches from Enoc Pena, an associate of Clase's, in 2023. De Aza Baez said the tips often came through a group chat titled "Uber Inc." that Pena started and included other men who have been referenced in the case and also worked for the ride-share company in Massachusetts at the time.

Prosecutors showed a screenshot of a text message Clase allegedly sent to Pena on Sept. 30, 2023, when the Guardians were scheduled to play the Detroit Tigers, that talked about "killing the first two chickens." De Aza Baez said the message was instructions to bet on a Clase pitch to the third batter of an inning, but only if Clase had retired the first two batters. Clase did not appear in the game.

Clase's defense has argued that mentions of roosters and chickens in such communications often were referencing cockfighting, a legal activity in the Dominican Republic, where Clase and others in the case are from.

De Aza Baez said he became friends with Pena as well as Robinson Vásquez Germosen and Luis Arismendy Paca Méndez, who are co-defendants in the case, while they were all living in Nantucket, Massachusetts. Paca Méndez, who has pleaded not guilty, is not participating in the trial after being extradited from the Dominican Republic to the U.S. on Oct. 19.

De Aza Baez said he met Clase when Vásquez and Pena brought the pitcher to his house for a birthday party on April 28, 2023, in Winthrop, Massachusetts, where De Aza Baez had moved. He met Clase again a few days later at a relative's house. Prosecutors showed a video of the gathering, with Clase playing dominoes on a table featuring a Boston Red Sox logo. The Guardians were in town for a series against the Red Sox.

De Aza Baez said he never received any information directly from Clase, only from Pena. De Aza Baez said he did not have an agreement with Pena but gave him money because he "almost always" won using the information to bet on Clase's pitches. De Aza Baez acknowledged opening a DraftKings betting account under his wife's name to increase the amount he could wager and win on his Clase bets. De Aza Baez also said he included the Clase pitch bets in parlays to maximize payouts.

De Aza Baez acknowledged that he had agreed with the government to forfeit $69,000 from his winning bets on Clase and would "tell the truth" in exchange for prosecutors dropping a wire fraud charge related to the case.

Clase, Ortiz and Vásquez have pleaded not guilty to conspiracy charges of wire and honest services fraud, sports bribery and money laundering.

"Our defense is the same today as it was in opening: This is a case about big talk and small bets," Vásquez's attorney Todd Spodek told ESPN after Friday's hearing. "We're confident leaving that judgment to the jury."

The trial will continue next Thursday in Brooklyn.

stories.headline: Wings' Paige Bueckers, Azzi Fudd talk relationship on pod
stories.summary: Azzi Fudd hosted Wings teammate Paige Bueckers on her podcast and the two discussed their relationship, Dallas' season and Fudd's recovery from knee surgery.
stories.body:
Dallas Wings teammates Azzi Fudd and Paige Bueckers, the past two WNBA No. 1 draft picks, spoke on Fudd's podcast Friday about a variety of topics, including a personal life update.

"We're not together anymore; it's been a while," Bueckers said on the "Fudd Around and Find Out" podcast. "[We] share that because everybody [was] like, 'Oh my gosh, they're teammates, how is this going to work?'"

Bueckers and Fudd, who were teammates in college at UConn, said they felt the need to address their relationship status in part because of allegations it factored into the Wings picking Fudd at No. 1 in April. Fudd was chosen over TCU guard Olivia Miles, who went on to be the Rookie of the Year for the Minnesota Lynx. Spain's Awa Fam (Seattle Storm) was taken third, followed by teammates from the 2026 champion UCLA Bruins: Lauren Betts (Washington Mystics), Gabriela Jaquez (Chicago Sky) and Kiki Rice (Toronto Tempo).

Fudd, Fam, Betts and Miles were all No. 1 at different points in ESPN's mock draft in the months before the April draft. Bueckers said her previous relationship with Fudd had no impact on Dallas' decision.

"We were not together before she got drafted," Bueckers said. "She was not drafted because she was my girlfriend. She was drafted because she deserved it. She's an amazing human, an amazing basketball player. And we're still friends, we're still cool.

"We played an entire season together; we're the utmost professionals."

Fudd averaged 13.1 points but was limited to just 30 games after an injury to her right knee led to season-ending arthroscopic surgery in August. She offered an update on her health.

"My offseason's been good," Fudd said. "Lots of rehab, lots of training, lots of on-court workouts, lots of traveling. It's been busy.

"I think there's a lot I can improve on. Especially the iso game; I feel like I'm not too comfortable with that yet. I know I'm capable of doing a little bit more. Watching someone like Paige who is able to create from anywhere ... that's great inspiration for me."

Bueckers averaged 20.9 points, 4.1 rebounds and 5.9 assists, and was named to the All-WNBA second team as Dallas reached the playoffs as the No. 7 seed.

The Wings were eliminated in the first round by the eventual champion Golden State Valkyries. Bueckers said she learned a lot from her first playoff experience and complimented Golden State.

"The Valkyries' defense, I can't explain to you how tough they are," Bueckers said. "They swarm, they send bodies, they trap you, they blitz you, they're so connected. I'm glad I got to have that experience against them to open my eyes to what the playoffs are like -- the physicality, the pressure, the environment.

"And I'm proud of our season. I hated losing; I sat and was pissed about it for like a week. I reached out to [Sue Bird] about it, what was her first playoff experience like. I didn't play as well as I wanted to. But it was my first experience, going against a really good opponent, and I was learning and growing through it all."

Fudd and Bueckers also addressed the Wings' move to the 19,000-seat American Airlines Center in downtown Dallas next season after playing at UT Arlington's College Park Center, which seats over 7,000, since the franchise relocated to Texas in 2016.

"UTA was a vibe; we had a ball, we did our thing there," Bueckers said. "But definitely excited to move into Dallas. New times."

While the change in venue will lead to more eyes on Wings games, the two players said they're hoping for less scrutiny of any on-court behavior.

Both said fans shouldn't read into interactions the two have with each other or their teammates as anything other than normal team behavior. They also said they don't stand for "hate of any kind" or "tearing people down to lift us up."

"We've seen a lot of negativity," Bueckers said. "We've had stuff sent to us, stuff sent to our family, our friends. There's been some crazy things said about us. We still support each other, we're still going to be great friends, we're still going to be great teammates. All the negative things can be put aside, and you don't need to overanalyze everything."

Fudd added with a chuckle, "Also, we don't need messages [from fans] on what the other person's doing. We've addressed everything we need to, and the rest will stay with us."

stories.headline: Who should win 2026 MLS awards: Messi for MVP? Sullivan best young player?
stories.summary: With the MLS regular season coming to an end this weekend, ESPN asked its analysts to make their choices for the league's year-end awards.
stories.byline: Jeff Carlisle and Cesar Hernandez and Lizzy Becherano
stories.body:
The 2026 MLS regular season comes to a close Saturday. So much has happened in the 259 days since the campaign began -- there was a whole FIFA World Cup in the middle of the year, remember that? -- and that unpredictability has delivered some unexpected candidates for the league's year-end awards.

Back in February, who among us thought that then-16-year-old Cavan Sullivan would play at an MVP level? Who knew that Antoine Griezmann would hit the ground running upon his long-awaited arrival in North America? Who knew that former United States interim manager B.J. Callaghan would lead Nashville SC to the Supporters' Shield?

Although, there is always one constant you can count on: Lionel Messi playing at a level that no one has ever seen before in MLS.

So, on the eve of the season's final matchday, ESPN asked its writers: Who are you picking for this year's awards? Jeff Carlisle, Cesar Hernandez and Lizzy Becherano make their selections for coach of the year, young player of the year, newcomer of the year and Landon Donovan MVP.

Coach of the year

B.J. Callaghan, Nashville SC: This category is probably the toughest to pick. The midseason turnaround put in by the Philadelphia Union's interim manager Ryan Richter has been stunning. St. Louis City's Yoann Damet has accelerated the club's turnaround, with a 19-game unbeaten streak, and a U.S. Open Cup title, although they've faded of late.

Bruce Arena has gotten the San Jose Earthquakes back to the playoffs in his second season, no small feat given the club's usual level of ineptitude. The excellent season put in by FC Dallas' Eric Quill has flown under the radar. And then there's Callaghan, who now has a major trophy on his résumé with this year's Supporters' Shield triumph.

This probably comes down to a two-man race between Richter and Callaghan. My nod goes to Callaghan given Nashville is on the cusp of a record-setting points haul this season. -- Carlisle

Marko Mitrovic, New England Revolution: Expectations were modest, at best, for the Revs as they headed into 2026 under Mitrovic. Following a 2025 season that saw them once again miss out on the playoffs thanks to their 11th-place finish in the Eastern Conference, this year was anticipated to be more of a rebuild than anything else.

Instead, what followed was plenty of defensive solidity that propelled them up to their fourth place in the Supporters' Shield standings. In attacking support, Mitrovic has also gotten the best out of Carles Gil, who leads the team in goal contributions with 25. After a few years coaching within the U.S. youth international structure, Mitrovic is now thriving at the senior level. -- Hernandez

B.J. Callaghan, Nashville SC: Callaghan undoubtedly deserves this trophy for the incredible work he's done with Nashville. The team lifted the Supporters' Shield and tied Miami's MLS regular-season points record with one game left in the campaign. He's elevated the club since joining in 2024, taking a good roster to a trophy-winning club.

"B.J. is an excellent coach, very talented coach," said Hany Mukhtar. "What impresses me most is that he's always willing to improve -- constantly willing to improve the team, constantly willing to adjust and make players better and better and better. And that is, I think, the culture at this club." -- Becherano

Young player of the year

Cavan Sullivan, Philadelphia Union: I would be shocked if my colleagues selected anybody else. Once only on the radar of American soccer nerds, Sullivan has rapidly transitioned from teenage prospect to a genuine elite MLS player in 2026.

What's especially exciting about the 17-year-old is that he's not only shining on the stats sheet with his goals and playmaking, but also showing off a compelling level of tenacity and fight for a player who is still technically a kid. He's a joy to watch, and it's only a matter of time before the rest of the world learns about the creative yet daring attack-minded player and future U.S. men's national team star. -- Hernandez

Julian Hall, Red Bull New York: This is a tough award to give with so much rising talent between Sullivan, Hall and Justin Ellis, but I have the Red Bull New York striker just narrowly edging out the others. He's developed steadily over the years, really breaking out this season under head coach Michael Bradley.

Hall has 13 goals and five assists in 31 games, becoming an integral part of the Red Bull roster. Hall also became the youngest player in MLS history to record a hat trick, doing so at 18 years and 50 days. He has so much potential to tap into yet, but he's already showing signs of stardom. -- Becherano

Cavan Sullivan, Philadelphia Union: The amount of attention attached to Sullivan's arrival in MLS as a 14-year-old would have sunk just about any player in the league at the same age. Two years on, he's grown to the point that he's begun exceeding the hype.

His six goals and ten assists in league play since the World Cup break have played a huge part in the Union's second-half revival, in which they rose from rock bottom of the league-wide standings to clinching a playoff spot. The only question heading into Decision Day is which team Philadelphia will play in the postseason. Even better, Sullivan has done it with a style that has generated a tidal wave of excitement over just how much he'll grow in the coming years. -- Carlisle

Newcomer of the year

Antoine Griezmann, Orlando City SC: Many questioned what version of Griezmann would arrive in Orlando after years of wanting to play in the U.S., but he quickly proved that he came to MLS to compete. Although he signed in March, he didn't join the team until July following the end of the LaLiga season. It took him little time to adjust, scoring just 48 minutes into his debut.

Since then, Griezmann has gone on to record 14 goals and eight assists in just 17 games. His contributions propelled Orlando from 12th place, sitting outside the playoffs upon his arrival, to clinching a place in the 2026 postseason. -- Becherano

Antoine Griezmann, Orlando City SC: This award looks to be a two-horse race. Do you go with the season-long excellence of the Houston Dynamo's Guilherme, and his 16 goals and 10 assists? Or do you opt for the second-half supernova that was Griezmann, with his 14 goals and eight assists?

Both players have vastly outperformed their xG+xA, with Guilherme by almost 13 goal contributions while Griezmann has nine more than expected, but it's hard to look past the fact that the France World Cup winner's numbers have come in about 1,000 fewer minutes. Orlando has also resurrected its playoff chances with Griezmann in the lineup, clinching a spot on Sunday. Those last two factors mean that Griezmann just edges out Guilherme for the award. -- Carlisle

Guilherme, Houston Dynamo: Some players need weeks, if not months, to adjust to MLS. Guilherme needed 66 minutes. Scoring in the second half of his debut match for Houston in February, the Brazilian then doubled the mark with a game winner that cemented a brace in his first-ever MLS game -- which foreshadowed what would eventually follow.

Since then, the 31-year-old has continued to be highly efficient with 16 goals and 10 assists across his 30 appearances. Although things have slowed down for a Houston side that have just one win in their past nine, they could still become dark horses in the playoffs if they have a healthy and fit Guilherme in the XI. -- Hernandez

Landon Donovan MVP

Lionel Messi, Inter Miami: Is there really any other choice? Numbers-wise, the Argentina World Cup winner has practically lapped the field with 26 goals and 16 assists, and Miami has done well enough as a team to make Messi's contributions vital.

To be clear, other players had outstanding seasons. There remains a chance that the best player on the best team, that being Nashville SC's Hany Mukhtar, will get some votes, but his 17 goals and eight assists don't stack up to Messi. Neither do the 14 goals and 17 assists that Evander put up for an inconsistent FC Cincinnati side. Had Griezmann been with the club for a whole season, he might have threatened Messi for MVP supremacy. But as it stands, Messi is the clear choice. -- Carlisle

Lionel Messi, Inter Miami: Surprise, surprise. Sure, there are plenty who will justifiably wonder if this is simply just a popularity vote when he once again wins this award, but the numbers don't lie.

Messi leads the league in goals, goal contributions and xA. Diving into American Soccer Analysis' Goals Added metric, which "measures a player's total on-ball contribution in attack and defense," the Argentine superstar is head and shoulders above every other player in MLS with a tally of 14.06. For reference, at second place is San Jose Earthquakes forward Preston Judd, with a tally of 4.37. No matter the fact that he'll turn 40 next year, Messi continues to be the most dominant figure in MLS. -- Hernandez

Lionel Messi, Inter Miami: For a third consecutive season, Messi deserves the MVP award. He's recorded 26 goals and 16 assists in 30 games, carrying Inter Miami to second in the Eastern Conference, the Campeones Cup win over Cruz Azul and yet another Concacaf Champions Cup qualification.

Beyond the goals and assists, Messi's vision and IQ transform Inter Miami. The Herons struggled with consistency this season, playing under three coaches in the span of one campaign, but despite the constant chopping and changing, Messi remained the only positive constant. MLS may just have to change the name of the award given that Landon Donovan only won it twice. -- Becherano

stories.headline: Does Man United's coach matter? Could Jurgen Klopp reach Premier League glory at Old Trafford?
stories.summary: If Manchester United hired an all-time great like Jurgen Klopp, would they have won the Premier League? Let's find out!
stories.body:
Right around this time every year, you can start to feel it. The air gets a little crisper. The shadows get a little colder. The days get shorter. The tree colors start to pop. You start wearing sweaters. Pumpkins appear in places where they do and do not belong.

Everyone and everything starts to shift, just slightly, in preparation for what's about to happen. The cycles of nature can be fickle and unpredictable, so the date is never exactly the same, and some years come and go without anything at all. But most years, it does.

Our tiny little rituals prime us to anticipate the inevitable, oncoming shift: that moment when Manchester United fire their manager and convince themselves that the new guy is finally going to be the one who fixes everything.

Ruben Amorim lost his job last January. Erik ten Hag was fired two years ago, right before Halloween. Ole Gunnar Solskjaer got the boot just a couple of days before Thanksgiving. And Jose Mourinho was relieved of his duties a little over a week before Christmas.

Now that we've once again entered the season of sacking, Michael Carrick seems like he will inevitably become the latest victim.

Man United are clear of the relegation zone on goal differential alone. If history is any indication, their comeback against AS Roma in the Champions League will end up being meaningless. Before Tuesday's win, Carrick appeared to be on the verge of tears at the end of every match.

This is the 14th season since Manchester United last won the Premier League. And whoever replaces Carrick will be the ninth coach to try to do something that no other United manager since has done: just, simply, meet the expectations at one of the richest sports teams on the planet for more than a single season in a row.

But given how many different coaches have now failed since Sir Alex Ferguson left the club, it makes you wonder: Could anyone have been successful at Manchester United?

What is a great manager worth?

Arsenal won the Premier League last season with 85 points.

If we lived in a world where there were no subs and everyone on the field contributed exactly evenly to their team's success, then all 11 Arsenal players would have contributed about 8 points (7.7, to be slightly more exact) of value last season.

Except, the alternative to each player isn't just zero points. If you removed Bukayo Saka from the lineup, you wouldn't have to play a man down. No, you'd get to put another player out there who would also contribute to winning to some degree.

So, let's look at the relegation-level cutoff. West Ham were relegated with 39 points. Using the same framework, we'd say that all of their players were worth a little over 3.5 points across the season. We could then say that the average Arsenal player provided 5 more points of value than a relegation-level player.

This, of course, isn't exactly how it works: Some players are better than others, some positions are more valuable than others, and almost nobody plays 100% of the minutes. Goalkeeper David Raya played 97.3% of the league minutes last season, and Declan Rice led all outfield Gunners with 90.5% of minutes played.

But it all still gives us a nice benchmark. The best players on the best teams in the world are probably worth around 7 points more than your average relegation-level player. The truly generational superstars? You could probably bump that number up to 10 points if you wanted to.

But what about the manager? Rather than litigating the whole "managers don't matter" conversation for the 1,000th time on this website, we're just going to go with the logic put forth by Liverpool's former director of research, Ian Graham, in his book, "How to Win the Premier League": "[About] the same value as a good player brings. This is in line with manager salaries -- the best managers are paid a similar wage to the best players."

Who, then, was the best manager that Manchester United could've hired at any point over the past 14 seasons?

Most soccer-watchers would agree that there are two potential answers: Pep Guardiola or Jurgen Klopp. And most analyses would agree.

A 2025 study from the Sloan Sports Analytics conference looked at team performances from 2017 through 2024 across Europe's Big Five top leagues. The study awarded or penalized the manager for how much a team's performance level exceeded or undershot expectations based on the talent of the roster. Klopp and Guardiola topped the list -- with a significant gap between themselves and the next tier of coaches.

Given the 114 guilty charges against Manchester City under Guardiola, though, I think we have to go with Klopp. While Guardiola's influence on how the sport is played is undeniable, we now have to look on his Man City tenure skeptically. We know how much they outperformed what we were told they spent, but it would be foolish to blindly accept those numbers and attribute the gap purely to the Guardiola effect.

With Klopp, though, we know that he turned two clubs that were not even the richest clubs in their own leagues into two of the best teams in the world. And we know that he maintained those levels -- at both clubs -- for many seasons in a row. On top of that, both Borussia Dortmund and now Liverpool seem to have gotten worse after he left each job.

The job of the manager, simply, is to make his team better than the talent his club can afford to acquire and then to keep that improvement going even as the roster turns over. At the highest level of the sport, Klopp was better at that than any of his peers.

Could the best manager in the world save Manchester United?

What, then, might've happened if Manchester United somehow managed to hire Jurgen Klopp back in 2013 instead of David Moyes?

There are, of course, all kinds of ripple effects we could tease out -- what it would've done to German soccer, where Liverpool would've ended up, how Mohamed Salah's career would've played out, and on and on.

But I just want to focus on what it would've meant for Manchester United. We know that Liverpool benefitted from hiring Jurgen Klopp. But we also know that Jurgen Klopp benefitted from working for a club that did things like convincing him to sign Mohamed Salah instead of Julian Brandt.

Liverpool's cutting-edge front office didn't turn the club into the best team in the world, and neither did Klopp. No, it was the combo of the two that did it.

We could say similarly about Borussia Dortmund. At the time, Dortmund were one of the leaders in both youth development and identifying young stars. This meant that Klopp got the ideal kinds of talent, energetic youngsters to play his high-pressing style: Robert Lewandowski, Mats Hummels, Marco Reus, and Ilkay Gündogan -- just to name a few.

What we know about Manchester United, broadly, is that the club is an abject disaster. In terms of doing things that increase their chances of winning games, they are pretty much as bad as it gets. Since 2013, United have finished at or higher in the table than their relative Premier League revenue ranking once -- and that was last season.

While we could employ some magical thinking and convince ourselves that the only problem here is that the club can't hire the right coach, that's obviously not true. If it were, it would mean that the club that keeps firing its coaches just so happens to be doing all of the other things right.

No, the failure to find a successful long-term coach is a symptom of all of the other issues that plague the club. They've so badly underperformed their resources for over a decade; we can confidently say there is something deeply wrong with the way Manchester United tries to build its soccer teams.

So, if Klopp were the Man United coach, he wouldn't have fixed all of those problems. No, he would've had to work within that dysfunctional environment. He would've, in other words, ended up with Brandt instead of Salah -- many times over.

But let's sketch out the absolute best-case scenario for this hypothetical. Let's say that United have continued to hire "relegation-quality" managers. And let's say that Klopp's value is equivalent not just to the best player on a title team but to a true, once-in-a-generation superstar.

Neither of those things is true -- United aren't constantly hiring genuinely bad coaches, and Klopp himself would tell you that he's not worth the same as Lionel Messi -- but stretching the effect out to the extreme helps make the point.

Plus, by applying a Messi-like effect every year, we're canceling out some of the other problems with this exercise: not addressing the Manchester City situation, not subtracting points from other teams, not accounting for the increased spending power from an increased performance level, and so on.

If Klopp could've added 10 points to every Manchester United season, here's how things would've changed:

On average, United would've ended up with 76 points per season instead of 66, and their average finishing position would've been 3.8 instead of 5.3.

So, of course: things would be better if Manchester United had employed the best manager of the modern era for the last decade-plus. In this scenario, they would've finished in the top four 10 times, rather than six. Perhaps there would've been a deep Champions League run at a club that reached three finals in four seasons from 2008 to 2011 and hasn't been beyond the quarterfinals since.

But even if we granted Manchester United 13 straight seasons of consistent, transformative, incomparable, once-in-a-generation managerial performance, the team would still find itself right where it sits today: with no Premier League titles since Sir Alex Ferguson left the club.

stories.headline: The Philippine legend who keeps Jonny Parsons going
stories.summary: Philippine hero Lapu-Lapu defeated Ferdinand Magellan at the Battle of Mactan in 1521, and the story carries a personal meaning for Jonny Parsons that he takes with him every time he steps into the Octagon.
stories.body:
More than 500 years after Lapu-Lapu defeated Ferdinand Magellan at the Battle of Mactan, his legacy continues to inspire generations of Filipinos.

For UFC fighter Jonny Parsons, that story carries a personal meaning that he takes with him every time he steps into the Octagon.

Parsons, a Filipino-American whose mother is from Cebu, learned about the legendary warrior only in 2020, well into his mixed martial arts career. But once he discovered Lapu-Lapu's story, he found a connection to the resilience and spirit that have become part of his identity as a fighter.

"I have the warrior spirit," Parsons told ESPN. "My mom is from Cebu, so I have that Lapu-Lapu fighting spirit in me.

"It's definitely about resilience and holding it down for your people."

On April 27, 1521, Lapu-Lapu led native warriors against Magellan's forces at the Battle of Mactan in the Visayan islands of the Philippines. Using their knowledge of the terrain, the defenders overcame the Portuguese explorer's armed expedition and killed Magellan, disrupting Portugal's efforts to establish control over the islands.

Lapu-Lapu's victory remains a defining moment in Philippine history. He is celebrated as a symbol of Filipino resistance, courage and independence.

Parsons will carry that same resolve into his next challenge. The 35-year-old is set to face José Souza in a welterweight bout at UFC Fight Night: Cortes-Acosta vs. Walker.

"It's just a great story about overcoming the odds," Parsons said.

"They won that battle against Magellan, and in [Lapu-Lapu's] lifetime, the Philippines wasn't conquered. It wasn't until years after he was gone that they were conquered.

"I definitely want to say that my fighting spirit comes from that side of the family."

Parsons will have his own odds to overcome against Souza, as the Brazilian stands 6-foot-3 and holds a 10-inch reach advantage over the 5-foot-9 Parsons.

Souza, 24, carries a 9-1 professional record and is 1-0 in the UFC. On the other hand, Parsons owns a 9-3 record, including a 1-0 mark in the UFC.

The Filipino-American is returning from a layoff of 40 months after persistent hip flexor and groin injuries disrupted his training and kept him away from competition.

Still, he believes he has the tools to deal with the physical disadvantage and make a statement in his return.

"I'm no stranger to fighting a taller, longer opponent," he said.

"I think I have all the tools and weapons to defeat this guy [Souza].

"It just means that everyone's going to be able to see the best Jonny Parsons so far. But not the best ever, because I'm still getting better."

The extended break did not mean stepping away from the sport. Parsons, who is also now a mixed martial arts coach, kept training, shifting his focus to building strength, improving his conditioning, and addressing the physical issues that had held him back.

"This whole time that I've been off, I've been training," he told ESPN.

"I've been focusing on my strength and conditioning to help mend injuries and certain problem areas that were giving me issues during training.

"So I would say right now, I'm the healthiest and strongest I've ever been."

The experience also forced Parsons to rethink how he prepares for fights.

Rather than pushing through every session, he learned to treat recovery as seriously as training to develop a more disciplined approach to keeping his body healthy.

"I put a very heavy emphasis on my strength and conditioning training here in Vegas at the Performance Institute," he said.

"I also put much more effort into my recovery. Sometimes recovery, well, actually all the time, recovery is not just laying in bed and resting.

"Recovery is stretching. Recovery is a cold plunge, a sauna and walking. So I've really developed a much smarter training regimen that has allowed me to train at a very high level while avoiding all types of injuries."

Parsons is ready to show what that patience and discipline have produced.

"I'm very calm when I go into fights, and I'm very peaceful. I know I fight the best when I'm at peace. And it's very easy for me now to find that peace."

stories.headline: Ponga stars as NZ book Cup final spot with Tonga win
stories.summary: New Zealand are into their first World Cup final in 13 years after Kalyn Ponga returned from a broken arm to power the Kiwis past Tonga in a 34-10 win.
stories.body:
New Zealand are into their first World Cup final in 13 years after Kalyn Ponga returned from a broken arm to power the Kiwis past Tonga in a 34-10 win.

At a McDonald Jones Stadium dominated by Tongan flags, Ponga marked his comeback from a 23-day absence with a broken arm with an influential performance in Saturday's semi-final.

The Newcastle fullback set up three of the Kiwis' six tries and pulled off one of the try-saving tackles of the tournament as New Zealand advanced to next Sunday's final in Brisbane.

The Kiwis, who also welcomed back hooker Phoenix Crossland following his lengthy suspension, will learn their opponents on Sunday when Australia face Samoa in the other semi-final.

On the other side of the coin, this was a missed opportunity for Tonga who have failed to reach a single final across three-straight tournaments.

Fullback Lehi Hopoate made five errors and the Tongan halves struggled to master the elements, particularly in the second half when they were running into a ferocious wind.

This semi-final exit is likely to mark the last chance for Jason Taumalolo - the architect of rugby league's Pacific revolution - to win a World Cup.

But there remains a chance for New Zealand to become world champions next week after Ponga marked his return with a protective arm guard to send Briton Nikora crashing over after three minutes.

Tonga soon hit back as Jojo Fifita started and finished one of the most breathtaking tries of the tournament.

Catching a bomb five metres off his own line, the Gold Coast winger surged through a gap in the Kiwis' kick chase, linked with Tui Lolohea and Tolu Koula, who burned Joe Tapine and turned the pass back infield for Fifita to score.

Ponga halted Demitric Vaimauga with an incredible last-gasp tackle to slow Tonga's charge, before Fifita muscled over on the left for his second of the night.

Isaiya Katoa couldn't make the conversion and that was as close as Tonga got to victory.

As halftime approached, the Kiwis edged ahead 12-10 courtesy of Dane Gagai and never looked back.

Hopoate was unable to deal with a bouncing ball to the in-goal under pressure from Ponga and Gagai pounced.

But Tonga were unable to go the distance as Casey McLean, Jahrome Hughes, Xavier Willison and Charnze Nicoll-Klokstad moved New Zealand out of sight with second-half tries.

stories.headline: Max Verstappen, Lewis Hamilton, Charles Leclerc to take grid penalties in Brazil
stories.summary: Max Verstappen and both Ferrari drivers will incur grid penalties at the São Paulo Grand Prix after new power unit components were fitted to their cars ahead of Saturday's qualifying session at Interlagos.
stories.body:
Max Verstappen and both Ferrari drivers will incur grid penalties at the São Paulo Grand Prix after new power unit components were fitted to their cars ahead of Saturday's qualifying session at Interlagos.

Verstappen will start from the back of the grid after exceeding his season-long quota for internal combustion engines, turbochargers and exhausts with replacement parts fitted to his Red Bull ahead of final practice.

Lewis Hamilton and Ferrari teammate Charles Leclerc are both set for 10-place grid penalties after the Italian team exceeded its quota for internal combustion engines on both cars.

There had been speculation that Ferrari would stagger the changes on Hamilton and Leclerc's cars over the next two races to reduce the chances of their drivers starting next to each other on the grid, but the identical penalties in São Paulo mean that is not the case.

Hamilton, Leclerc and team principal Fred Vasseur held clear-the-air talks on Thursday evening in Brazil after an incident between the pair on the opening lap of the Mexico City Grand Prix saw both drivers' chances of victory heavily compromised.

The problems may extend beyond the grid penalty for Hamilton after he reported smoke in his cockpit during final practice and returned to the pits with 25 minutes remaining.

Mercedes driver George Russell is also facing a five-place grid penalty after his team fitted the second internal combustion engine beyond his quota for the season on Friday.

- F1 to make a decision on season finale in Imola next week - sources

- Charles Leclerc says 'everything is settled' after Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari crisis talks

- Max Verstappen tops final practice; starts São Paulo GP from back of grid

Cadillac driver Sergio Pérez is also due to start from the back of the grid after his team changed the Ferrari internal combustion engine, turbocharger and MGU-K on his car ahead of final practice on Saturday.

The various penalties will be applied to the grid after Saturday's qualifying.

stories.headline: Unai Emery: Michael Carrick's Man United the 'same level' as Barcelona
stories.summary: Aston Villa boss Unai Emery has said that Manchester United are the "same level as Barcelona," insisting Michael Carrick's side present a tough challenge.
stories.body:
Aston Villa boss Unai Emery has said that Manchester United are the "same level as Barcelona," insisting Michael Carrick's out-of-form side present a "very difficult" challenge.

Villa travel to take on United on Sunday, bidding to extend their five-game unbeaten run while piling the pressure on Carrick, who has managed just one league win all season.

Emery's record at Old Trafford makes for pretty dismal reading, however, having never won there during his managerial career. Villa, meanwhile, have lost each of their last six meetings there in all competitions.

Therefore, on the back of Villa's 3-0 Champions League defeat to LaLiga champions Barcelona, Emery has been talking up United.

"We performed like we planned [against Barcelona] but it was not enough, because the level we were facing, this is the highest level for the Premier League and Champions League matches," Emery said.

"On Sunday, Manchester United -- it's the same level as Barcelona. So this is the work we are trying to set with the players, of course very, very demanding."

He added: "It's Manchester United and we have very clear samples, we didn't win one match there for four years. So it means for us it's very difficult.

"Manchester United is a fantastic club, they are performing very good, last year they achieved to play the Champions League. In the league they started not being consistent, but they should recover their consistency. So it's a very, very difficult match."

Emery, who has confirmed he is in talks over a new contract at Villa, stressed his side will have to be at their best.

- Man United approaching a crossroads: Back Carrick, or move on?

- Man United's Baleba set for lengthy spell out with injury

- JJ Gabriel amid Madrid move talk: 'Dream to win Ballon d'Or'

"Old Trafford is a huge challenge -- for me, for the players, for our trajectory here together, because we are not winning there.

"We have had some hard defeats, like two years ago when we were close on the last match, to get to the Champions League, and we lost. We lost it.

"So, it's always very, very difficult there. We must play our best -- in our best individual and collective way.

"So, we have a lot of work to do, and we must compete at the same time."

Information from PA contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Luka Doncic's 53-point explosion pushes scoring average past 40 as Lakers roll
stories.summary: Luka Doncic poured in a season-high 53 points in a 124-118 win over the Trail Blazers, raising his scoring average to 40.1 PPG.
stories.body:
LOS ANGELES -- Though Michael Jordan, Kobe Bryant and James Harden came somewhat close, no NBA player has averaged at least 40 points in a season since Wilt Chamberlain in 1962-63.

Through his first nine games of the season, Los Angeles Lakers star Luka Doncic is on pace to reach that historic benchmark thanks to his latest 50-point explosion.

Doncic poured in a season-high 53 points to lead the Lakers to a 124-118 victory over the Portland Trail Blazers at Crypto.com Arena on Friday. The Slovenian star is averaging a career-high 40.1 points per game as he captains the NBA's No. 1 offense.

"Luka can do some things that maybe a handful, if not no one, can do in basketball," Lakers coach JJ Redick said.

Chamberlain is the only player to score more than Doncic's 361 points through his first nine games in a season. The Hall of Fame center had 472 points through nine games in 1962-63 and 455 points in the 1961-62 season, according to ESPN Research.

Chamberlain went on to average an NBA record 50.4 points in 1961-62 and 44.8 points in 1962-63. Jordan's 37.1 points per game in 1986-87 is the NBA's highest mark during the 3-point era, Harden's 36.1 points per game in 2018-19 was the most prolific scoring season of the 21st century, and Bryant's 35.4 points were the most by a Lakers player since the NBA/ABA merger in 1976.

Can Doncic, whose career high for a season is 33.9 points per game with the 2023-24 Dallas Mavericks, join Chamberlain in averaging at least 40 points?

"It's obviously a long season," Doncic said. "We're 10 games in. We've got 72 left. As long as we're winning, I'm good. I got [the shots] up today, I'm not going to lie. Hopefully, it continues, but you never know."

Doncic, 27, is taking full advantage of his new role as the undisputed face of the Lakers after LeBron James' offseason departure to the Philadelphia 76ers. Entering Friday, Doncic was leading the league in scoring, shot attempts, 3-point attempts, free throw attempts, usage rate, player efficiency rating and win shares.

Against the Trail Blazers, Doncic exceeded 40 points for the sixth time this season and topped 50 for the second time. He ranks tied for 10th all time with 11 career 50-point games and is fifth among active players, trailing only Harden, Stephen Curry, Damian Lillard and James.

Doncic, whose 62-foot heave at the halftime buzzer keyed Friday's comeback win, joined Bryant, Elgin Baylor and George Mikan as the only Lakers to score at least 40 points in four consecutive games.

"[Doncic] is the MVP right now," Trail Blazers coach Micah Nori said during his pregame comments. "Hands down."
